blindness_statement: Only the specified keyless worksheet was read as source material. No answer map, source code, repository evidence, or other agent work was consulted.
scale_assumption: Difficulty 2–3 is interpreted as ordinal levels on a 1–5 scale because the worksheet specifies no separate rubric.

conclusions.note_on_larger_roots: Every item includes its larger root as a choice; that choice satisfies the equation but does not answer the minimum question.
conclusions.set_level_judgment: All eight items are the same exercise template. They support factorization/minimum-root practice, but provide little variety for assessing distinct reasoning. Once the first item is learned, the remaining items likely feel easier than their standalone ratings.

items.independent_math: x² − 17x + 60 = (x − 5)(x − 12) = 0. Thus x = 5 or 12; both lie in [0, 14], and the minimum is 5.
items.difficulty_basis: Requires factoring a monic quadratic into two integer roots, then applying the minimum qualifier. Arithmetic is small enough for hand work.
items.teaching_note: A teacher can use the larger root distractor to check whether students distinguish satisfying the equation from answering the minimum question, and the adjacent values to probe substitution/factoring errors.
